front: An engineer deposits \(\text{\$8{,}000}\) in an account earning \(6\%\) compounded annually. What is the account worth after \(10\) years?
explanation: 1) Use the single-payment compound-amount factor \((F/P, i, n) = (1+i)^n\). 2) \((1.06)^{10} = 1.7908\). 3) \(F = P(1+i)^n = \text{\$8{,}000}\times 1.7908 \approx \text{\$14{,}327}\).

front: How much must be deposited today in an account earning \(8\%\) compounded annually to grow to \(\text{\$50{,}000}\) in \(15\) years?
A new machine is expected to save \(\text{\$12{,}000}\) per year for \(8\) years. At an interest rate of \(10\%\), what is the present worth of these savings?
A \(\text{\$30{,}000}\) loan is repaid in equal end-of-year payments over \(5\) years at an interest rate of \(9\%\). What is the annual payment?
\(\text{\$5{,}000}\) is deposited at the end of each year for \(12\) years into an account earning \(7\%\) compounded annually. What is the future worth of the deposits?
How much must be deposited at the end of each year to accumulate \(\text{\$100{,}000}\) in \(10\) years, if the account earns \(6\%\) compounded annually?

Maintenance on a generator costs \(\text{\$1{,}000}\) at the end of year \(1\) and increases by \(\text{\$200}\) each year through year \(5\). At \(10\%\) interest, what is the present worth of the maintenance costs?

A cash flow is \(\text{\$0}\) in year \(1\) and increases by \(\text{\$500}\) each year through year \(6\) (that is, \(\text{\$0}, \text{\$500}, \ldots, \text{\$2{,}500}\)). At \(8\%\) interest, what equivalent uniform annual amount is this series worth?
explanation: 1) A pure arithmetic gradient converts to a uniform series with \((A/G, i, n) = \dfrac{1}{i} - \dfrac{n}{(1+i)^n - 1}\). 2) \((A/G, 8\%, 6) = \dfrac{1}{0.08} - \dfrac{6}{(1.08)^6 - 1} = 12.5 - 10.224 = 2.2763\). 3) \(A = G(A/G, 8\%, 6) = \text{\$500}\times 2.2763 \approx \text{\$1{,}138}\).

front: A credit card charges a nominal annual interest rate of \(18\%\) compounded monthly. What is the effective annual interest rate?
An investment of \(\text{\$10{,}000}\) today returns a single lump sum of \(\text{\$16{,}105}\) at the end of \(5\) years. What annual rate of return does it earn?

A machine costs \(\text{\$60{,}000}\), has a salvage value of \(\text{\$10{,}000}\), and a useful life of \(5\) years. Using straight-line depreciation, what is the book value at the end of year \(3\)?
explanation: 1) Straight-line annual depreciation: \(D = \dfrac{\text{cost} - \text{salvage}}{n} = \dfrac{\text{\$60{,}000} - \text{\$10{,}000}}{5} = \text{\$10{,}000}\) per year. 2) Accumulated depreciation after \(3\) years \(= 3\times\text{\$10{,}000} = \text{\$30{,}000}\). 3) \(BV_3 = \text{\$60{,}000} - \text{\$30{,}000} = \text{\$30{,}000}\).

front: A \(\text{\$40{,}000}\) asset has a \(5\)-year depreciable life. Using the double-declining-balance (\(200\%\) DB) method, what is the depreciation charge in year \(2\)?
explanation: 1) Double-declining-balance rate: \(d = \dfrac{2}{n} = \dfrac{2}{5} = 0.40\), applied to the beginning-of-year book value. 2) Year 1: \(D_1 = 0.40\times\text{\$40{,}000} = \text{\$16{,}000}\), so \(BV_1 = \text{\$24{,}000}\). 3) Year 2: \(D_2 = 0.40\times\text{\$24{,}000} = \text{\$9{,}600}\).

front: A highway project has a present worth of user benefits of \(\text{\$5{,}000{,}000}\), present-worth disbenefits of \(\text{\$500{,}000}\), and a present worth of costs of \(\text{\$3{,}000{,}000}\). Using the conventional benefit-cost ratio, is the project justified?
explanation: 1) The conventional benefit-cost ratio nets disbenefits against benefits: \(B/C = \dfrac{\text{benefits} - \text{disbenefits}}{\text{costs}}\). 2) \(B/C = \dfrac{\text{\$5{,}000{,}000} - \text{\$500{,}000}}{\text{\$3{,}000{,}000}} = \dfrac{\text{\$4{,}500{,}000}}{\text{\$3{,}000{,}000}} = 1.5\). 3) Since \(1.5 > 1\), the project is economically justified.

front: A monument costs \(\text{\$2{,}000{,}000}\) to construct and \(\text{\$40{,}000}\) per year to maintain in perpetuity. At an interest rate of \(4\%\), what is its capitalized cost?
explanation: 1) Capitalized cost is the first cost plus the present worth of perpetual annual costs: \(CC = P_0 + \dfrac{A}{i}\). 2) \(\dfrac{A}{i} = \dfrac{\text{\$40{,}000}}{0.04} = \text{\$1{,}000{,}000}\). 3) \(CC = \text{\$2{,}000{,}000} + \text{\$1{,}000{,}000} = \text{\$3{,}000{,}000}\).

front: A scholarship fund will pay \(\text{\$10{,}000}\) per year for \(4\) years, with the first payment at the end of year \(6\) (payments in years \(6, 7, 8, 9\)). At \(8\%\) interest, what single amount today is equivalent to the fund?
explanation: 1) Value the 4-payment annuity one period before its first payment (end of year \(5\)) with \((P/A, 8\%, 4) = 3.3121\): \(P_5 = \text{\$10{,}000}\times 3.3121 = \text{\$33{,}121}\). 2) Discount back \(5\) years with \((P/F, 8\%, 5) = 0.6806\). 3) \(P_0 = \text{\$33{,}121}\times 0.6806 \approx \text{\$22{,}542}\).
